name: Taiwan
headline: Taiwan's single insurer offers every insured person three years of claims-based records online, with 12.48 million registered users, but full charts stay in each hospital.

access.summary: The Medical Care Act gives a right to a copy of the record, and My Health Bank shows three years of visits, medicines, lab results and imaging reports to 12.48 million registered users. Copies cost the patient, and Liberty Times reported only 1 to 3 million regular users.
detail: Article 71 of the Medical Care Act says a facility must give the patient a copy of the record on request, with a Chinese summary when needed, and may not delay or refuse without reason. The patient pays the cost. The Act sets no deadline in days, though the privacy law's 15-day reply rule also applies.

My Health Bank, built by the NHIA in September 2014, shows the last three years of Western, Chinese medicine and dental visits, inpatient stays, surgery, medicines, allergies, lab results, imaging or pathology reports and discharge summaries. It also links vaccination records, organ donation and hospice wishes, and cancer screening results.

The NHIA said on 28 March 2026 that registered users passed 12.48 million and queries passed 600 million. The same day Liberty Times reported about 1 to 3 million regular users, after a surge during the pandemic.
Because the portal is built from claims, it does not carry full clinical notes or records older than three years. Those still come from each hospital, on paper or disc, at the patient's cost.

control.summary: A person can set an NHI card password that stops all contracted doctors and pharmacists from viewing their MediCloud data, and a separate opt-out covers research use. The block is a single switch that must be set in person at an NHIA or district office.
detail: The NHIA says anyone can set an NHI card password at its offices or local district offices. Once set, clinicians cannot query the person's MediCloud records. Providers may not force the patient to reveal the password or refuse care because of it.

The NHIA warns that the choice trades privacy against safety, since the doctor then loses the cross-provider view. The control is a single switch. There is no option to hide one visit, one test or one provider.

Since August 2025 the NHIA has also let people stop research and other secondary use of their NHI data, by app or at a counter, choosing among four data types. The NHI Data Management Act put this right in law. It does not cover claims processing or internal NHIA work.

MediCloud queries need three cards: the facility's security module, the clinician's card and the patient's NHI card. Whether patients can see a list of who viewed their MediCloud record was not verified in this review.

privacy.summary: Medical records are a special category under the Personal Data Protection Act, but the independent commission named in the law still does not exist, and sector ministries enforce with fines of NT$50,000 to 500,000. Ransomware attacks in 2025 exposed about 16.6 million patient records.
detail: Article 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act bars collecting or using medical, genetic and health check data except in listed cases, such as written consent or a legal duty. People may ask to see, copy, correct or delete their data, and requests must be answered within 15 days, extendable once.

The law in force only requires telling the person after a breach caused by a violation. A November 2025 amendment adds reporting duties and new fines for failing to report, but the Personal Data Protection Commission says its start date will be set later by the Executive Yuan.

The Commission was legally due by 12 August 2025, after a 2022 Constitutional Court ruling on the NHI database. As of August 2026, its organic act had sat in the legislature for over 300 days, so enforcement stays split across ministries.

Prosecutors said in June 2026 that attacks on Mackay Memorial Hospital, Changhua Christian Hospital and a company in early 2025 leaked about 16.6 million patient records, and charged two men for buying Mackay records to resell. The Medical Care Act was last amended on 23 September 2026.

commercial.summary: The NHI Data Management Act bars secondary use of insurance data for commercial profit and limits applicants to government, hospitals, universities and research bodies. Hospital records and consumer apps outside the NHI database fall back on the general privacy law and its small fines.
detail: Article 8 limits secondary use of NHI data to care quality, health equity, public health, welfare, research and statutory duties, and says applications may not be for commercial profit. Article 9 limits applicants to public bodies and domestic hospitals, research institutes and universities.

Article 15 requires a share of any industry profit earned within 15 years from approved research to be paid into the NHI fund. Unapproved use draws a fine of NT$2 million to 10 million and a one-year ban.

Outside the NHI database, the Personal Data Protection Act needs written consent for health data, and firms must stop marketing when a person objects. Fines for misusing health data run NT$50,000 to 500,000.
Taiwan has no EU adequacy decision, so EU organisations need other safeguards to send personal data, including health data, to Taiwan.

journey.summary: One insurer contracts with about 93% of providers, including every hospital, and NHI MediCloud pools 13 types of data plus CT and MRI images from all of them. Full hospital charts are only now being linked through FHIR, with clinics due in 2028.
detail: The NHIA says it contracts with about 93% of medical institutions: 100% of hospitals, 92.6% of primary clinics and 79.3% of pharmacies. Claims flow to one payer, which feeds MediCloud.

MediCloud holds Western and Chinese medicines, tests and results, surgery, dental care, drug allergies, controlled drugs, clotting factor drugs, rehabilitation, discharge summaries, special materials and CDC vaccination records. Since 2018 CT, MRI, ultrasound, endoscopy and X-ray images can be shared.

MOHW plans to link full electronic records through FHIR: medical centres in 2026, regional and district hospitals in 2027, and health stations and clinics in 2028. It relies on insurance payment incentives rather than penalties.
E-prescriptions are early. By mid-October 2025, 282 facilities had passed the NHIA's technical review, and National Taiwan University Hospital issued its first in January 2026.

clinical.summary: Any contracted doctor or pharmacist can see a patient's medicines, results, discharge summaries and images from other providers through MediCloud once the patient's card is inserted. Results and images go back only 12 months, and full notes from other hospitals are not yet shared.
detail: A MediCloud query needs the facility's security card, the clinician's card and the patient's NHI card. It returns test results and medical images from the last 12 months, plus recent medicines and other records.

Since 2018 the system warns about duplicate prescriptions across hospitals, drug interactions and drug allergies. Clinics can view CT and MRI images taken at large hospitals, which saves patients NT$200 to 600 per disc.
Hospitals that want to download a patient's records in bulk before a visit need the patient's written consent and must delete the data after the visit.

Full charts are not shared across hospitals yet. MOHW said in April 2026 that from May, referred patients at linked medical centres would no longer need to carry discs. An emergency rule for patients who have set a card password was not verified.

research.summary: Researchers keep access to near-national insurance data, but since August 2026 the law lets anyone opt out of all or part of it, with public lists of approved projects. By September 2026, 24,511 people, about 1 in 1,000, had opted out.
detail: The NHI Data Management Act took effect on 10 August 2026. Anyone who did not opt out in the first 30 days is deemed to consent, but can opt out later. Opt-out is not retroactive and does not bind government bodies with a statutory duty to obtain data.

Review committees must be at least half experts, civic groups and independent members. Data are pseudonymised, used in secure sites, and results must not identify anyone. Approved case lists and result reports must be published.

The NHIA lets people choose among four data types and two kinds of user. MOHW told a hearing on 16 September 2026 that 24,511 people had opted out, and said cancer registry, screening, death and electronic record data still need their own rules and consistent standards.
For studies on people, the Human Subjects Research Act requires ethics committee approval and informed consent that can be withdrawn at any time, unless the authority has exempted a study type.

ai.summary: Clinical AI software is a medical device that needs TFDA approval, and changes to listed items need approval too. The AI-specific change plan route (2024) and machine learning principles (2026) are guidance, not law, so Taiwan sits low in the device-regulation band.
detail: The Medical Devices Act (2020) counts software as a medical device, requires registration before manufacture or import, and requires approval for changes to designated registration items.

TFDA issued AI and machine learning device software review guidance in September 2020, a predetermined change control plan guide in September 2024, and good machine learning practice principles in June 2026, covering product design, software quality, training and test data, clinical evaluation and post-market monitoring. All are issued as administrative guidance.
MOHW's generative AI guideline for medical institutions (29 May 2026) says qualified clinicians make the final decision, patients should be told, and recording stops if a patient refuses.
The AI Basic Act (14 January 2026) sets seven principles, including human oversight and transparency, and requires warnings on AI that ministries and the digital ministry deem high risk.
